title: Recovery of centered normalized towers by restriction and local flat tests
statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced Noetherian scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth]. A centered normalized blowup tower $B$ retains its coherent defining ideal $J_i$ at each stage $X_i$ [def-trf-normalized-blowup]; assume all its intermediate schemes are Noetherian. Define $\operatorname{Ass}(B)$ to be the union of the images in $X$ of the associated points of $\mathcal O_{X_i}/J_i$, where an associated point is one whose local maximal ideal annihilates a nonzero element of this quotient.

Let $j:U\to X$ be a quasi-compact flat monomorphism (the diagonal is an isomorphism), and suppose $\operatorname{Ass}(B)\subset j(U)$. Then $B$ is uniquely recovered from its uncontracted restriction $j^*B$ by taking schematic closures of its centers at each successive normalized blowup stage. For a restricted closed centre $Z$, schematic closure means the closed subscheme defined by $\ker(\mathcal O\to j_*\mathcal O_Z)$ on the corresponding stage. Thus if two such towers have equal uncontracted restrictions and both associated-point sets lie in $j(U)$, they have equal lengths and equal ordered ideal centers on $X$. This applies in particular to the rational localization $X_{\mathbf Q}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$, whether or not it is an open subscheme.

Equality of two centered towers can also be tested after an fpqc cover (a faithfully flat quasi-compact morphism) whenever their scheme-theoretic uncontracted pullbacks exist. If $X$ is nonempty, it can be tested after the family $\{\operatorname{Spec}\widehat{\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{X,\bar x}}\to X\}_{\bar x}$ of completed strict local schemes, again assuming these uncontracted pullbacks exist [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The maps $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\widehat{\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{X,\bar x}}$ are faithfully flat local maps. In particular a nonempty centre having a point over $x$ has nonempty pullback to this completed strict local scheme. When $X$ is empty, the completed-strict-local family is empty and equality of the original tower lengths must be required separately; with this length comparison the same test applies. These tests compare the actual ideal sheaves and the original finite stage indices, without deleting unit-center stages. Noetherian schemes here admit finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings.

proof.text: Put $U_i=X_i\times_XU$ and $j_i:U_i\to X_i$. A pullback of a monomorphism is a monomorphism (its diagonal is the pullback of the original diagonal); flatness is preserved by base change [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and quasi-compactness is preserved by base change [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change]. By [lem-per-flat-monomorphism-local-structure], $U_i$ is reduced and Noetherian, $j_i$ is regular, and its local ring maps are isomorphisms. Thus [lem-per-normalized-tower-regular-pullback], specifically its second paragraph for arbitrary reduced Noetherian bases, identifies the recursive normalized tower on $U$ with these scheme-theoretic pullbacks and the extended ideal centers. It retains exactly the original finite index set.

Fix $i$ and cover $X_i$ by finitely many affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A'$ with $A'$ Noetherian (the stages are Noetherian). Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a principal open $D(g)$ of one of them, so $A=A'_g$ is again Noetherian (every ideal of $A'_g$ is extended from $A'$); these $V$ form a basis of the topology of $X_i$. Write $I=J_i(V)$. Suppose $a\in A$ vanishes on the restriction of the closed center to $j_i^{-1}V$. For every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_A(A/I)$, [lem-sfb-affine-associated-points-primes] applied to $\mathcal O_{X_i}/J_i$ makes the corresponding point $z\in V$ an associated point of that quotient. Its image in $X$ lies in $j(U)$ by the hypothesis on $\operatorname{Ass}(B)$. The fibre description in [lem-per-flat-monomorphism-local-structure] therefore supplies a point $u\in U_i$ over $z$, with an isomorphism of local rings. Modulo $J_i$, this identifies the restricted center stalk at $u$ with $(A/I)_{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently the class of $a$ is zero in every such localization. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-injects-localizations-associated-primes] it is zero in $A/I$, hence $a\in I$. Conversely every element of $I$ vanishes on the restricted center by its definition. This proves the equality of sections on every such $V$, a basis of opens, hence as ideal sheaves, $J_i=\ker(\mathcal O_{X_i}\to(j_i)_*\mathcal O_{Z_i\times_XU})$.

proof.text: Recover the tower by induction on its original stage index. At index zero its ambient scheme is $X$. Given the reconstructed $X_i$, the preceding kernel formula recovers $J_i$ from the restricted center, and [def-trf-normalized-blowup] constructs $X_{i+1}$ from exactly this ideal. The initial identification and each successor identification are therefore canonical. If two uncontracted restrictions agree, their finite lengths already agree, and this induction gives equal ordered ideals and stages. A unit ideal remains a recorded ideal at its original index, including a stage whose normalized blowup is the identity.

For the rational localization, on $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ the inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}(S^{-1}A)$, where $S$ is the image of the nonzero integers. This is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. It is a monomorphism because the multiplication map $S^{-1}A\otimes_A S^{-1}A\to S^{-1}A$ has inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$: every $1\otimes s^{-1}$ equals $s^{-1}\otimes1$. It is affine, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. The preceding reconstruction consequently applies with $U=X_{\mathbf Q}$ under its stated associated-point hypothesis, without an openness hypothesis.

source.place: VIII proof of Theorem 3.4.15, p.114 (recovery from the rational localization)

proof.text: First consider ideals $I,J$ on a scheme $T$ and a jointly surjective flat family $T_a\to T$ on which their extended ideals agree. For $t\in T$, choose a lift $v\in T_a$. The local ring map $\mathcal O_{T,t}\to\mathcal O_{T_a,v}$ is flat and local, hence faithfully flat by [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective]. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction], contraction of the equal extended stalk ideals gives $I_t=J_t$; equality at all stalks gives equality of ideal sheaves. For an fpqc cover $Y\to X$ and a point $z\in X_i$ over $x\in X$, choose $v\in Y$ over $x$. The flat local map $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{Y,v}$ is faithfully flat by the same local-flat lemma. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum], $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(z)\otimes_A\mathcal O_{Y,v})$ is nonempty; its points give lifts of $z$ to $X_i\times_XY$. Thus every stage cover is surjective, and it is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. Uncontracted equality after the cover includes equality of lengths even on the empty scheme. Starting at $X_0=X$, apply the ideal argument and construct the next normalized blowup from the common ideal [def-trf-normalized-blowup]. Induction gives equality whenever the assumed scheme-theoretic pullbacks exist.

For $x\in X$ with geometric point $\bar x$, choose an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}D\ni x$ from a finite cover by spectra of Noetherian rings and set $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}=D_{\mathfrak p}$, a Noetherian local ring. By [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] there is a $D$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{X,\bar x}\cong A^{\rm sh}$, compatible with the structural morphism to $X$ and with residue fields, where $A^{\rm sh}$ is the pair colimit over etale $A$-algebras $S$ with $A$-maps $\chi:S\to K$, $K$ the separable closure of $\kappa(x)$ in $\Omega$. Sending $(S,\chi)$ to the triple $(S,\ker\chi,\bar\chi)$ (the prime $\ker\chi$ lies over $\mathfrak m_A$ because $A\to K$ kills $\mathfrak m_A$) and a triple $(S,\mathfrak q,\phi)$ to $(S,\phi\circ(S\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)))$ is an isomorphism of index categories compatible with the diagrams, so $A^{\rm sh}$ is also the triple colimit used below. Since $\theta$ is a local isomorphism it identifies the completions at the maximal ideals; put $C=\widehat{A^{\rm sh}}\cong\widehat{\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{X,\bar x}}$.

source.place: Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring); algebra.tex Tag 04GW (lemma-strict-henselization-different) for the pair/triple colimit models

proof.text: With $A$, $A^{\rm sh}$ and $C$ as in the preceding step: The local maps $A\to A^{\rm sh}$ and $A^{\rm sh}\to C$ are faithfully flat by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat] and [lem-sc-strict-henselization-completion-noetherian]. Their composite is faithfully flat: tensoring successively preserves and reflects exactness, which is precisely [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. It is also local. For any point $y\in X_i$ with image $x$, base change to $\kappa(y)$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change]; its spectrum is nonempty by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum]. Thus the completed-strict-local family, after pullback, is jointly surjective on every stage; it is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. Apply the ideal and induction argument of the preceding step. When $X\ne\varnothing$, at least one geometric point exists and equality of that uncontracted pullback also forces equal lengths. When $X=\varnothing$, the explicit length comparison in the corrected statement supplies this datum; there is only one ideal on each empty stage. Finally, if a center has a point $y$ over $x$, the same nonempty spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(y)\otimes_A C)$ maps into its pullback, proving the asserted nonemptiness. No stage is contracted.
